materials.title: A film without dialogue
materials.text:
Last Friday, our film club ____1____ (watch) a short silent comedy. At first I was disappointed because I wanted to hear what the characters were saying. Our teacher asked us to notice how much information came from their ____2____ (face) and movements.

The main character was a waiter ____3____ carried too many plates at once. Every time someone opened the kitchen door, he had to change direction. We could understand his problem without ____4____ (hear) a single word.

Afterwards, we worked in groups to make a short scene of our own. My group decided ____5____ (show) a person trying to catch a bus. We did not have a real bus, so we used three chairs and a sign. A classmate held the sign while the rest of us acted.

Our first performance was difficult to follow. We moved too ____6____ (quick), and nobody knew who was waiting for whom. The second attempt was ____7____ (clear) than the first because we gave each movement a little more time.

At the end, we laughed ____8____ the funniest moments, including our own mistakes. The teacher did not choose a winning group. Instead, she asked each of ____9____ (we) which action had communicated the most. I left with ____10____ idea for another scene, this time about a visitor who could not find the right classroom.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 1 with the correct form of watch.
questions.explanation: Last Friday establishes a completed past event: watched. Watch is present/base; watching lacks an auxiliary.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 2 with the correct form of face.
questions.explanation: Their plural characters have faces. Singular face and activity facing do not name the several expressions observed.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 3 with one appropriate word.
questions.explanation: Who or that is the defining human relative subject. Which is nonhuman and whose would require a following possessed noun.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 4 with the correct form of hear.
questions.explanation: Without takes hearing. The base, finite past and to-infinitive forms do not complete this preposition.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 5 with the correct form of show.
questions.explanation: Decided takes the to-infinitive to show. Other listed forms do not fit directly.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 6 with the correct form of quick.
questions.explanation: Quickly modifies moved. Quickness is a noun. Informal flat-adverb quick is not automatically rejected.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 7 with the correct form of clear.
questions.explanation: Than requires a comparative: clearer or more clear. Clear lacks comparison, clearest is superlative and more clearer duplicates it.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 8 with one appropriate word.
questions.explanation: Laughed at the moments uses at. To, of and from do not complete this reaction construction.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 9 with the correct form of we.
questions.explanation: The preposition of takes object form us. We is subject form, our/ours possessive.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 10 with one appropriate word.
questions.explanation: An idea naturally introduces the proposed new scene and agrees with a vowel sound. A has wrong sound agreement; other unlisted article readings remain reviewable.

materials.title: The treasure stayed indoors
materials.text:
We had planned a treasure hunt in the garden for my sister's birthday. On Sunday morning, however, heavy rain ____1____ (change) our plans. Dad looked at the wet grass and suggested moving the game inside.

We needed new clues because the old ones mentioned trees and flowerpots. My sister helped us write ____2____ (they) on small cards. One card sent players to a shelf ____3____ held our family photographs. Another led to the cupboard under the stairs.

Before ____4____ (hide) the cards, we checked that nobody would need to climb on furniture. The game was for young children, so every clue had to be somewhere they could reach. We also decided ____5____ (leave) the kitchen out because Mum was preparing hot food there.

When the guests arrived, they worked in pairs. They read the cards ____6____ (careful), then ran to tell their partners where to look. We asked them to walk near the stairs, but they could move faster in the living room.

The treasure was a box of paper crowns. There were enough crowns ____7____ everyone, including two children who arrived late. My sister thought the indoor hunt was ____8____ (good) than our first plan. Nobody had muddy shoes, and the rain made the house feel like ____9____ adventure shelter. By the time we finished, all the ____10____ (child) were wearing their bright paper prizes.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 1 with the correct form of change.
questions.explanation: On Sunday morning in this past account, rain changed the plans. Base change and unaided changing do not fit.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 2 with the correct form of they.
questions.explanation: Write takes object pronoun them referring to new clues. They is subject, their possessive.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 3 with one appropriate word.
questions.explanation: The shelf is subject antecedent for that/which held. Where is not a subject; who refers to people, and what does not follow this expressed antecedent.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 4 with the correct form of hide.
questions.explanation: Before as preposition takes hiding. Other listed forms do not complete the -ing clause.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 5 with the correct form of leave.
questions.explanation: Decided takes to leave. The bare, -ing and past forms do not follow directly.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 6 with the correct form of careful.
questions.explanation: Carefully modifies read. Adjective and noun forms do not fit the adverb slot.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 7 with one appropriate word.
questions.explanation: Enough crowns for everyone states the recipients covered. Of, at and from do not express that sufficiency relationship.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 8 with the correct form of good.
questions.explanation: Than requires comparative better. Good is plain, best superlative and gooder nonstandard.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 9 with one appropriate word.
questions.explanation: An adventure shelter uses an before a vowel sound. A has incorrect sound agreement; unlisted article readings remain reviewable.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 10 with the correct form of child.
questions.explanation: All the children requires the irregular plural. Child is singular; childs is nonstandard.

materials.title: Air for the old bicycle
materials.text:
My cousin gave me an old bicycle, but one tyre was flat. On Saturday, I took it to a community workshop. A volunteer ____1____ (welcome) me and asked whether I wanted to learn how to use the pump myself.

First, she showed me the small valve ____2____ was hidden under a plastic cap. I put the cap in a bowl so that I would not lose it. Then we attached the pump and checked that it fitted ____3____ (safe).

I began to pump as fast as I could. The volunteer stopped me. Working more slowly made it ____4____ (easy) to watch the pressure than rushing did. She explained that the number printed on the tyre gave useful limits; guessing by how hard it felt was not enough.

After ____5____ (fill) the tyre, we removed the pump and replaced the cap. The wheel turned smoothly, but the volunteer reminded me that a full tyre did not prove the whole bicycle was ready to ride.

We looked ____6____ the brakes and lights as well. A second volunteer helped us check the other parts. I thanked both of ____7____ (they) for their time. I had expected a quick repair, but I left with ____8____ better understanding of what needed checking. Now I always ask for help if I am uncertain, rather than ____9____ (pretend) I know. The workshop also gave me a list of simple ____10____ (check) to keep beside the bike.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 1 with the correct form of welcome.
questions.explanation: On Saturday within this completed narrative, the volunteer welcomed the narrator. Other listed forms do not supply a past finite verb.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 2 with one appropriate word.
questions.explanation: That/which is the subject for valve in the defining relative clause. Who is human, where not subject, what incompatible with an explicit antecedent here.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 3 with the correct form of safe.
questions.explanation: Safely modifies fitted. Safety is a noun. Any unlisted alternative receives review rather than an automatic rejection.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 4 with the correct form of easy.
questions.explanation: Than rushing did creates a comparison requiring easier or more easy. Plain easy, superlative easiest and doubled more easier do not fit.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 5 with the correct form of fill.
questions.explanation: After as preposition takes filling. The bare, past and to-infinitive forms do not complete it.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 6 with one appropriate word.
questions.explanation: Looked at introduces the objects inspected. Of, from and by do not complete the intended inspection construction.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 7 with the correct form of they.
questions.explanation: Both of takes object pronoun them. They is subject and their/theirs possessive.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 8 with one appropriate word.
questions.explanation: A better understanding is the ordinary new-instance construction. An has incorrect sound agreement. Other article readings remain reviewable.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 9 with the correct form of pretend.
questions.explanation: Rather than can take pretending parallel with asking, or bare pretend after the earlier coordinated verb structure. Pretended does not fit the narrator’s general present habit.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 10 with the correct form of check.
questions.explanation: A list of simple checks uses plural count noun checks for several inspection actions. Check is singular without a determiner; checked is participle.

materials.title: A voice on the school radio
materials.text:
Our school radio team usually records short interviews. Last month, we ____1____ (ask) to make an announcement about a change to the sports day. Heavy rain was expected, so the outdoor events would take place on Friday instead of Thursday.

I wrote the first version, ____2____ contained every detail from the teacher's email. It was accurate but much too long. My partner suggested ____3____ (put) the new date at the beginning, where listeners were most likely to hear it.

We read the text aloud and timed ____4____ (we). Some sentences looked clear on paper but sounded confusing. For example, two different times appeared close together, and it was easy to remember the wrong one.

After we had made the wording ____5____ (simple), we asked a classmate to listen without seeing the script. She could repeat the date but was uncertain ____6____ where students should meet. That showed us which part needed another change.

The final announcement ____7____ (record) in a quiet room. We left a short pause after the important information and avoided background music. The teacher checked it before it was played.

Later, several students thanked us for speaking ____8____ (clear). They had heard the new arrangements while walking between lessons. I learned that writing for the ear was different ____9____ writing for the eye. A listener cannot always return to a sentence, so useful ____10____ (announce) need a clear order as well as correct facts.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 1 with the correct form of ask.
questions.explanation: The plural team members we receive the request last month: were asked. Asked lacks passive auxiliary, was disagrees and are uses present time.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 2 with one appropriate word.
questions.explanation: The comma introduces a non-defining clause referring to the version, so which. That does not introduce this non-defining clause, who is human and what lacks this antecedent relation.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 3 with the correct form of put.
questions.explanation: Suggested takes putting. Other listed forms do not directly fit.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 4 with the correct form of we.
questions.explanation: We timed ourselves, the same people reading and being timed. Subject and possessive forms do not supply the reflexive object.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 5 with the correct form of simple.
questions.explanation: Simpler or more simple states the improvement from the earlier version. Simplest is maximum, and more simpler doubles comparison. Plain simple is left reviewable as a valid resultative reading.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 6 with one appropriate word.
questions.explanation: Uncertain about where and uncertain of where both introduce the unknown meeting place. From/by do not complete this uncertainty construction.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 7 with the correct form of record.
questions.explanation: The singular announcement receives recording. Past or past-perfect passive can fit. Recorded lacks auxiliary; were disagrees.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 8 with the correct form of clear.
questions.explanation: Clearly modifies speaking. Clearness is a noun; informal clear is not automatically rejected.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 9 with one appropriate word.
questions.explanation: Different from, different to and different than are recognised variants here. Of and by do not express the comparison.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 10 with the correct form of announce.
questions.explanation: Need is plural here, so plural noun announcements. Base verb announce and participle announced do not name the items needing order.

materials.title: A notebook made by hand
materials.text:
At a weekend workshop, I learned to bind a small notebook. We began with sheets of paper ____1____ had been folded in half. The instructor asked us to check the edges before making holes for the thread.

My first set of holes was uneven. Instead of ____2____ (throw) the paper away, I used it to practise the next step. That allowed me to understand the movement before working on the final pages.

The thread passed through each hole twice. We had to pull it ____3____ (gentle), because too much force could tear the paper. I found the rhythm difficult at first, but it became ____4____ (easy) than I expected once I stopped watching everyone else.

Our instructor encouraged us ____5____ (choose) different covers. I used a piece of clean packaging with a blue pattern. Its folds were already visible, but I liked the way they became part of the design.

When the notebooks were finished, we placed ____6____ (they) on a table. No two looked exactly the same. One participant had added a pocket ____7____ the inside of the back cover, and she showed us how she had made it.

I wrote my name on the first page and left the rest blank. There was ____8____ sense of possibility in the small book. Later that evening, I ____9____ (fill) its opening pages with sketches of the workshop. The imperfect practice sheets stayed beside it, reminding me how much ____10____ (patient) a useful new skill could require.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 1 with one appropriate word.
questions.explanation: The sheets are subject antecedent of that/which had been folded. Who is human; where not subject; what does not take this expressed antecedent.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 2 with the correct form of throw.
questions.explanation: Instead of takes throwing. Other listed forms do not fit the preposition.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 3 with the correct form of gentle.
questions.explanation: Gently modifies pull. Gentle is adjective and gentleness noun.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 4 with the correct form of easy.
questions.explanation: Than requires the comparative easier or more easy. Plain, superlative and double comparative alternatives fail this structure.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 5 with the correct form of choose.
questions.explanation: Encouraged us takes to choose. Other listed forms do not directly complete this verb-object pattern.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 6 with the correct form of they.
questions.explanation: Placed takes object pronoun them for the notebooks. They is subject; their/theirs possessive.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 7 with one appropriate word.
questions.explanation: A pocket on the inside of a cover names the attachment surface. For, by and of do not express that placement.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 8 with one appropriate word.
questions.explanation: A sense of possibility is the ordinary new-feeling construction. An conflicts with the consonant sound of sense. Other article readings remain reviewable.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 9 with the correct form of fill.
questions.explanation: Later that evening is the completed past event filled. Base fill and unaided filling do not supply the finite narrative verb.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 10 with the correct form of patient.
questions.explanation: How much requires uncountable noun patience here. Patient is adjective and patiently adverb.

materials.title: The earlier ferry
materials.text:
Our family had booked an afternoon ferry for a day trip across the bay. The evening before, the operator sent a message ____1____ (explain) that strong winds were forecast for later in the day. We could travel on an earlier service or change the booking to another date.

Dad asked everyone ____2____ (check) the new departure time. We chose the early ferry because the operator said it was still scheduled to run, but we kept watching for updates. A forecast was not a promise that the conditions would remain unchanged.

At the terminal, the passengers ____3____ (direct) to a sheltered waiting area. A member of staff, ____4____ name badge read "Ruth", explained when boarding would begin. She answered our questions ____5____ (patient), including mine about whether the same ticket was valid.

The crossing was ____6____ (short) than I had imagined. From inside the cabin, I watched small waves pass the windows. We followed the crew's instructions and stayed away from the outside deck while it was closed.

On the island, we chose a walk near the village instead ____7____ climbing to the exposed viewpoint. We still enjoyed ____8____ (we), although the day differed from our first plan. Before returning, we checked the ferry notice once more. Flexibility had been ____9____ important part of the trip, and the clear ____10____ (message) from staff had made our choices easier.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 1 with the correct form of explain.
questions.explanation: Explaining describes the message’s content; to explain describes its purpose. Explained is passive without the required active content relation.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 2 with the correct form of check.
questions.explanation: Asked everyone takes to check. Bare, -ing and past forms do not directly fit.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 3 with the correct form of direct.
questions.explanation: Plural passengers receive direction. Past or past-perfect passive fits the narrative; directed alone lacks auxiliary and was disagrees.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 4 with one appropriate word.
questions.explanation: Whose modifies name badge possessively. Who, which and that cannot directly fill this possessive position.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 5 with the correct form of patient.
questions.explanation: Patiently modifies answered. Patient is adjective and patience noun.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 6 with the correct form of short.
questions.explanation: Than requires shorter or grammatical more short. Plain short and superlative shortest do not fit, nor double comparative more shorter.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 7 with one appropriate word.
questions.explanation: Instead of takes the -ing action climbing. To, with and at do not complete this construction.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 8 with the correct form of we.
questions.explanation: Enjoyed ourselves requires the reflexive object for the same family members. Subject and possessive forms do not fit.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 9 with one appropriate word.
questions.explanation: An important part is the ordinary newly introduced role and uses an before a vowel sound. A has incorrect sound agreement; other article readings remain reviewable.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 10 with the correct form of message.
questions.explanation: The several communications from the operator and staff are messages. Singular message without a determiner does not fit this noun phrase; messaging names an activity rather than the individual notices.
